result.summary: Applied REQ-237's .zig provenance-marking convention (lib/letflow/design/req237-zig-provenance-marking-convention.md, including its two 2026-09-05 amendments) to exactly the 7 files named in REQ-259 (chunk 239e2 of REQ-239's original scope): docs/migration/stage-{1,2,3,4,5,6,7}-*.md. 51 PROVENANCE marker lines inserted total across the 7 files (stage-1: 8, stage-2: 1, stage-3: 6, stage-4: 18, stage-5: 1, stage-6: 15, stage-7: 2), covering all 148 pre-existing .zig citation lines. Every citation unit was classified into one of the three documented markdown shapes: single citation line/bullet (e.g. stage-1's 'Key R-Co files' list, each bullet marked individually), paragraph bounded by blank lines (the majority of citations, including multi-line R-Co-source paragraphs and individual list-item paragraphs inside larger un-blank-separated lists such as the REVIEWER sign-off bullets in stage-4/stage-1), and whole-table (stage-4's five markdown tables, one marker per table above its header row, never per-row). No YAML-comment-line shape applies here (plain .md files only, per the task's own instruction) and none was used. No fourth/novel citation shape was encountered that did not fit one of the three documented shapes -- every citation resolved cleanly into single-line, paragraph, or table.

deviations_and_issues: No citation shape outside the three documented markdown unit types (single citation line/bullet, paragraph, table) was encountered anywhere in these 7 files. Several citations in stage-4-api-surface.md and stage-1-identity.md sit inside list items that are NOT separated from sibling list items by blank lines (e.g. stage-4's per-requirement REVIEWER sign-off bullets, stage-1's per-requirement verdict bullets, stage-6's numbered 'Deliberately not covered' items) -- each such bullet was treated as its own paragraph-shaped unit (marker placed immediately above the bullet's own '-'/'N.' marker), consistent with the design's stated rationale for the paragraph rule (avoids the judgement call of finding a sentence boundary inside dense prose) applied at the bullet-item granularity rather than the whole-list granularity, since bullets in a tight (non-blank-line-separated) list are still visually and semantically separate units, each citing different, independent R-Co source files. This is a mechanical extension of the paragraph rule to its most granular natural boundary (the list item), not a new shape -- flagging it here per the task's own instruction to record any judgement call rather than silently applying it, even though it did not require inventing new marker text or placement logic.

stage-4-api-surface.md's five markdown tables each required inserting a blank line before the marker (in addition to the marker line itself) where no blank line already separated the marker's insertion point from the preceding paragraph, to keep the table's own header row correctly recognized as a table by Markdown renderers immediately following the marker line. This added 4 extra blank-line insertions beyond the 18 marker lines (22 total insertions vs 18 markers) but does not touch, alter, or remove any existing citation text -- confirmed via the git diff --numstat and the -U0 .zig-line-touch check above.
